summary: super-color ships a Windows dropper that fetches and executes PE binaries from Discord CDN
details: The package presents itself as a color-printing library but conceals a Windows binary dropper inside its core API. On Windows (os.name=='nt'), calling Color.paint, Color.print, or Color.__call__ starts a background daemon thread ('sc-load') that downloads two PE executables from hardcoded Discord CDN URLs (cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/.../AVKiller.exe and.../bedwars.exe) into %TEMP%/SolaceRuntime using a urllib/curl/certutil fallback chain, then launches them with subprocess.Popen using the DETACHED_PROCESS creation flag. The file names and sequencing (an AV-killer executed before a second payload) indicate malware deployment. The fetch host is an anonymous mutable attachment CDN unrelated to any color-printing purpose, no hash or signature verification is performed, non-Windows platforms are silently bypassed to preserve the benign cover story, and the drop is triggered from the package's advertised API so any Windows caller that imports and uses the library executes the fetched binaries.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
